comparison.m4PrepareRecordNormal: M4 normal treatment used an eight-block packet and observer/decision/fallback surface. Codex used 16 tools, 285182 input tokens, and 90700 ms; Claude used 7 tools, USD 0.63906025, and 80369 ms.
comparison.narrowDecision: The minimum boundary is materially renderer-only: neither host used an observer, packet, decision hash, fallback, or prepare command, and both produced a canonical record with reread-observed effect. Tool count and Claude cost fell relative to the M4 normal treatment, while Codex wall time rose; therefore the gate supports proceeding to the Framework experiment but does not prove a general cost win or that this flow is cheaper than prose.

unknowns: Response-loss recovery is specified in the canonical entry and machine-tested through idempotent record, but this gate did not inject response loss into both hosts.
All non-normal record safety branches are machine evidence or retained M4 evidence, not fresh M5 host runs.
The two runs used byte-identical fixture inputs and the same operational request, but their raw prompt wording was not byte-identical; no cross-host causal cost comparison is claimed.
No L0/L1/L2 Framework behavior, unfamiliar authoring AI, or Product target is proven yet.
